name: Emotional responses to Beijing street scenes – 360° panoramas
description: Method replication: the task, questions and timing follow Zhang et al. (2021, IJERPH), but the images are not the paper's stimuli. In the original lab study, 26 participants wore a VR headset and saw 12 street panoramas of Beijing (small, medium and large streets); after looking around each scene for 30 s they answered three questions on interestingness (insipid / impassive / interesting), comfort (depressive / impassive / relaxed) and vitality (dull / impassive / vibrant), scored 1–3. Here each participant sees 12 of 87 Baidu street-view panoramas of central Beijing (hutong lanes to arterial roads), shown as wide 360° strips, for at least 30 s each, then answers the same three questions. Differences from the original study: (1) Baidu panoramas on a screen instead of the authors' own 360° photos in VR; (2) the physiological measures (EEG, skin conductance, heart rate) and the 30 s eyes-closed rest between scenes are not included.
author: Zhang, Zhuo, Wei, Li, Yin & Xu
